minutes.summary: A short Select Board meeting with only three members present. It held a public hearing on a Pride event, interviewed and appointed a Council on Aging member, and heard an update from the Historical Commission and APDC chair. The board approved a vacation payout for the town manager, rescheduled its workshop, and went into executive session on police union bargaining.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a payout of the town manager's unused FY22 vacation days instead of carrying them over; the vote had no opposition.
The board waived the liability insurance requirement and then approved the special event license for a Pride event on July 13 on the Ritter building lawn, both unanimously.
The board appointed James McGuigan to the Council on Aging for a term expiring June 30, 2024, unanimously.
The town was awarded a planning assistance grant for regional planning staff to help with MBTA zoning compliance, due to be completed by June 30, 2024.
With only three members present, the board postponed its policy workshop and deferred town manager and board goals until a full board is seated.

why_it_matters: The vacation payout is a cost to the town budget, which is mostly taxes, and the board chose it over carrying the days forward.
The MBTA zoning grant bears on a rule the town must meet by mid-2024, and it may lead to a zoning vote at a later Town Meeting.
The board postponed its goals and policy workshop, so the priorities that guide the next budget cycle are not yet set.
watch_next: July 12 workshop on policy articles one and two, and a regular meeting on July 19; the July 5 meeting may be cancelled.
Whether the Historical Commission and APDC bring a budget request to the board this fall, before the town manager's budget process.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the insurance waiver, the McGuigan appointment, the vacation payout and the warrant amounts.
